headline: Real Madrid chase Rodri as Maresca era begins at City
paragraphs: Real Madrid's interest in Manchester City's Rodri remains the best-corroborated transfer story in the feed. Sky Transfers reported Madrid are working on a deal for the midfielder, and BBC's gossip column separately said Madrid are confident of signing him. That BBC line was also carried by BBC Sport, the same newsroom rather than extra confirmation, but Sky's report is a genuinely separate outlet. Nothing is signed, and both accounts remain rumour, not an announced deal.

Away from the transfer market, Manchester City's managerial change is already settled fact: Sky reports Enzo Maresca held his first press conference as City manager, succeeding Pep Guardiola, saying he would not be a "copy and paste" coach. Separately, Sky reported Real Madrid had an £85m bid rejected by RB Leipzig for winger Yan Diomande, whom the outlet also describes as a Liverpool target, raising the possibility the two clubs end up chasing the same player.

Arsenal's news was thinner and single-sourced. BBC's gossip column, in the same round-up as the Rodri line, linked the club with Manchester City's John Stones and Aston Villa's Ezri Konsa as possible defensive cover, and reported Real Madrid are open to selling Aurelien Tchouameni to Manchester United. None of that is corroborated elsewhere in the feed, so treat it as gossip rather than a developing deal.
